families.source: UKHSA communicable disease outbreak management guidance collection
families.topic: the official outbreak-management principles, toolkits and implementation resources for local health protection systems
evidence_points: The collection brings together principles and toolkits for identification and management of communicable-disease outbreaks.
It is intended to support local health protection system responses in England.
The collection complements disease-specific and organisation-specific guidance rather than replacing it.
It includes resources on risk assessment, incident management teams, investigation, communications, debriefing, reporting and audit.
The material was developed by UKHSA with NHS England and wider system partners.
The landing page records updates made in July 2026 to roles, legislation, whole-genome sequencing, health equity and IMT resources.
The page is an official GOV.UK source for the official outbreak-management principles, toolkits and implementation resources for local health protection systems and was live-checked on 31 July 2026.
The source is intended to support evidence-based, proportionate action and should be used with current local and topic-specific arrangements.
A notification, case, cluster, symptom, setting issue or checklist alone does not establish that every recommendation in Communicable disease outbreak management guidance applies.
Final decisions require current incident facts, responsible-authority judgement, documented risk assessment and any applicable clinical, legal or operational evidence.

families.source: UKHSA principles for local communicable disease outbreak management
families.topic: outbreak definitions, preparedness, investigation, control, communication, equity, stand-down and audit
families.page_title: Communicable disease outbreak management guidance: principles to support local health protection systems
evidence_points: The guidance defines an outbreak as at least 2 linked people affected by the same infectious disease or agent.
It also treats some single rare or high-consequence cases and contamination events as outbreak-like incidents.
Outbreak management begins with identification, initial investigation and risk assessment.
Investigation may combine epidemiological, microbiological, environmental, food-chain and veterinary evidence.
Control measures, communication and engagement should be reviewed dynamically until the outbreak ends.
The guidance expects local plans, notification pathways, training, exercises and data-sharing arrangements to support preparedness.

families.topic: regional and national UKHSA roles and functions supporting local outbreak management
evidence_points: The toolkit summarises UKHSA structures and functions relevant to local outbreak management.
It distinguishes regional UKHSA services from national UKHSA services.
Health protection teams provide local operational health-protection response and advice.
Field Services support epidemiological investigation, surveillance and analysis.
Reference and specialist microbiology services can support organism characterisation and outbreak evidence.
National incident structures may support escalation when an incident exceeds routine local arrangements.

families.topic: the statutory duties, powers and legal frameworks relevant to communicable-disease outbreak response
families.page_title: Toolkit 2: summary of health protection legislation
evidence_points: The toolkit summarises legislation relevant to outbreak identification, investigation and control.
It supports understanding of organisational duties and available health-protection powers.
Notification duties form part of the legal framework for detecting notifiable disease and organisms.
Local authorities, UKHSA, NHS organisations and other responders have different statutory functions.
Legal powers should be applied through appropriate governance and proportionality.
The summary supports but does not replace legal advice on a specific incident.

families.topic: dynamic communicable-disease outbreak risk assessment and control-strategy review
evidence_points: The toolkit provides approaches to outbreak risk assessment and a communicable-disease risk-management model.
Risk assessment should begin early in an outbreak.
Risk assessments should be reviewed regularly as evidence and circumstances change.
Assessment outcomes should inform investigation and control strategies.
The chosen framework should fit the circumstances and be agreed by the incident management team.
The assessment approach and outcome should be documented.
